lane: CAM-UV: Andrey against lingam 1.13.0, causal-learn 0.1.4.8, and the empty graph
build: Andrey pre-release build of the 0.13.0 branch, 1 November 2026
source: Maeda and Shimizu (2021), Causal additive models with unobserved variables, UAI, PMLR 161, 97-106: the model of Sect. 2 and the simulation of Sect. 5.1, at the settings of Sect. 5
fit_protocol: one timed fit per dataset, no warm-up, one BLAS thread on one core, four fits at a time on four cores, a 3600 s wall cap per fit; *_cpu_s are the medians of the fits' CPU time, cpu_ratio the median over the paired datasets of the reference's CPU time over Andrey's, with its bootstrap 95% interval
error_metric: direct_errors: the directed edges claimed against the edges between observed variables that no unobserved causal or backdoor path joins, the edges CAM-UV can identify as direct; a missing or extra edge costs 1 and a reversed one 2. shd_endpoint: the endpoint SHD against the PAG of the observed variables. shd_endpoint_bidirected: the same with the estimate's marked pairs drawn <->, the references' mark (Andrey draws o-o), so the two packages' graphs are compared without the mark convention. pair_precision and pair_recall: the marked pairs against the pairs an unobserved causal or backdoor path joins, pooled over the datasets of a cell. same_graph: the same directed edges and the same marked pairs, whatever the mark; same_marks: the same endpoint marks
verdict_rule: D = direct_errors(Andrey) - direct_errors(reference) per dataset on the datasets both finished; the mean D with its percentile bootstrap 95% interval (10,000 resamples); a cell in claim is worse when the interval lies above 0, better when below, a tie otherwise; a cell worse or better is run again on 20 fresh seeds (20-39, the replication rows) and keeps its verdict only if the replication's interval lies on the same side of 0 (final_verdict). Cells with claim 'out' are reported, not judged
seeds_note: 20 datasets per cell in claim (seeds 0-19), 10 per cell out of claim (seeds 0-9), and replications on seeds 20-39; a seed whose graph cannot hide its nodes is skipped and the next one taken, which no cell of this campaign needed

settings.andrey: andrey.camuv defaults: alpha 0.01, max_depth 2 (sets of up to 3 variables)
settings.mapping: lingam CAMUV(alpha=alpha, num_explanatory_vals=max_depth + 1); causal-learn CAMUV.execute(X, alpha, max_depth + 1); their pairs drawn <->

regimes.latent_anm_er: additive noise X_c = sum w g(X_p) + e with g(z) = z + sin(z), Gaussian noise, Erdos-Renyi graph of mean degree 2, standardized; one node in five hidden, chosen among nodes with two or more children; 2,000 rows (in claim)
regimes.latent_anm_er_tenth: the same model with one node in ten hidden, one per ten observed; 1,000 rows (in claim)
regimes.camuv_paper: the paper's simulation: 10 observed variables, each pair joined with probability 0.3, two hidden common causes into two observed variables each, two hidden intermediates each in place of an observed edge, effects (v + a)^c + b with c in {2, 3}, uniform noise, each variable divided by its standard deviation (in claim)
regimes.anm_er: additive noise with nothing hidden, 20 variables, 1,000 rows (out of claim)
regimes.latent_gauss_er: linear Gaussian, one node in ten hidden, 20 observed variables, 1,000 rows (out of claim: linear effects)

differences.method: each dataset where Andrey's graph differs from a reference's, whatever the mark, is refitted along one path of switches from lingam's CAMUV to Andrey's: lingam on the columns in Andrey's rank order (the order its sets are visited in), then with Andrey's HSIC test, then with Andrey's regressions, then Andrey's engine with lingam's algorithm (a variable's non-parents removed together, no edge on a directed cycle dropped), then Andrey's phase 2 (one candidate at a time), then the cycle drop, which is andrey.camuv. first_switch counts, per cell, the switch after which the graph is Andrey's; switch_changed_graph the datasets where each switch changes the graph. A dataset where the references differ is refitted with causal-learn using lingam's HSIC test. At 50 observed variables 5 of the 20 datasets are traced (seeds 0, 1, 5, 10, 15)
differences.same_parts_same_graph: lingam's code with Andrey's test and regressions returns the graph of Andrey's engine with lingam's algorithm on every traced dataset, so each difference is made of the five switches and nothing else
differences.references: causal-learn with lingam's HSIC test returns lingam's graph on every traced dataset where the two differ: their difference is the HSIC test, whose bandwidth reads every row in causal-learn and the first 100 rows in lingam
differences.two_cycles: no traced lingam fit made two variables each other's parent, which the adapters' marks would hold as one edge
differences.marks: with marks as returned, Andrey's o-o and the references' <->, two graphs are the same only where neither marks a pair (same_marks); same_graph reads the pairs whatever the mark
